body.statement: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^K\) and a fixed admissible law \(P_0\), viewed as the constant sequence \(P_n=P_0\), with \(\mu_n=\mu_0\) and \(\Omega_n=\Omega_0\). Suppose ass:iid-triangular-sampling, ass:primitive-moment-envelope, ass:primitive-covariance, and ass:regular-primitive-map hold; \(d_i(\mu_0)\ne0\) for every \(i\in V\); \(d_j(\mu_0)^2-d_k(\mu_0)^2\ne0\) for every \((j,k)\in\vec E\); the lower and upper endpoint problems defining \(\psi_q(\mu_0)\) have uniquely winning component-sign branches and unique primal--dual bases; and their branch-selection, primal-slack, dual-slack, and reduced-cost margins are strictly positive. Then a neighborhood of \(\mu_0\) has the same ratio ordering, winning branches, and primal--dual bases, and \(\psi_q\) is continuously differentiable there by the active-basis or KKT formula composed with \(\Gamma\). Consequently, \(\sqrt n\{\psi_q(\bar h_n)-\psi_q(\mu_0)\}=J_q(\mu_0)\sqrt n(\bar h_n-\mu_0)+o_{P_0}(1)\Rightarrow N(0,J_q(\mu_0)\Omega_0J_q(\mu_0)^\top)\). For every \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\) with \(\sqrt n\,\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), \(\widehat J_{q,n}\to_{P_0}J_q(\mu_0)\). If both diagonal entries of \(J_q(\mu_0)\Omega_0J_q(\mu_0)^\top\) are positive, each lower or upper endpoint of \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{ND}}\) differs from its corresponding known-cell oracle endpoint in \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{or}}\) by \(o_{P_0}(n^{-1/2})\). This conclusion is pointwise at \(P_0\).
body.justification: Strict branch and basis margins turn the apparently nonsmooth endpoint problem into one stable differentiable cell and certify first-order oracle behavior there.
body.gap: HongLi2018 establishes numerical-delta validity for directionally differentiable maps, while FangSantos2019 characterizes bootstrap behavior at nondifferentiable maps; neither derives the fixed-cell Jacobian, basis-stability neighborhood, and oracle-equivalent endpoint intervals for this componentwise supershort union.
body.consumer: In regular ACS specifications, software can report short Gaussian endpoint intervals with a theorem identifying exactly when they coincide to first order with a known-branch, known-basis oracle.
